brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Seamline, the open-source command-line tool in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: precise, trustworthy, developer-native; it must work in a terminal-heavy README, as a GitHub avatar and on a small docs site. No database cylinders, no elephants, no generic terminal prompt. Web and GitHub only.

claim.notes: Hiçbir konsept kalite kapısını geçemedi: join kör puanları 6 olsa da "sunulur mu" sorusuna hayır aldı ("CU"/boru dirseği okuması), s-weave 4-5 aldı, steps eskiz turunda iki kez elendi; iki tur sonunda durdum.

concepts.title: Unbroken Join
readsAs: an orange pipe elbow running between two black brackets (plumbing fitting)
the letters C and U side by side ('CU')
a cable connector or bracket clamp from a UI icon set
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 align/distribute-centre icon (bar through offset blocks), struck; s2 square split by a stepped cut, puzzle/Z channel, generic cut device, struck; s3 one black line jogging between two offset plates, a Z-shaped trace or wire, closest to the idea (the join that never breaks); s4 align-centre-vertical icon with a pole through bars, struck. Keep in s3: a single unbroken ink line that changes rows without breaking, plates sliding apart around it. Fix: the jog currently reads as a Z/zigzag and the four floating plates as a UI align glyph; reduce to two plates (old/new schema) so the line clearly passes the seam between them, give the line a distinct, deliberate turn (not a generic step), and make the black/orange contrast survive 16 px where it now becomes stripes. Avoid any arrowhead reading.

concepts.title: Seam stitch
readsAs: a chain-link / broken-link icon (two blocks with a diagonal bar across the gap)
a pixel-font 8 or a split S
a hinge or bolted bracket with a slash through it
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 two adhesive bandages on a tile (medical, and the pills zigzag into an S; 77% stock); s2 a sutured diagonal / band-aid across a square, medical; s3 two offset panels bridged by one bar, a connector/joint; s4 an X close button in a rounded square (UI icon, struck). Keep s3: the only one whose first reading is two parts held level across a seam, which fits continuity and lines up with small steps. Risks: the bar reads as a generic pill/link connector rather than a stitch, and two offset rectangles plus a bar is generic geometry. Fix: make the bridge read as thread (needle holes or a visible pass through both panels), keep the gap clearly a seam, tune the offset so it reads as one step not a broken tile, and prove it in one colour at 16 px and as a 40 px avatar. No bandage cues.

concepts.title: Small Steps
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a tilted pause icon / double slash (and a sliced block, the cut cliche); s2 a hamburger menu in a circle, the stock striped-disc logo; s3 a flattened Tetris S piece or a step-line chart glyph; s4 a Tetris Z tetromino. All four still read as stock interface/game shapes; s3 comes closest to the idea (one continuous band, one step) but its first reading is a step function or tetromino, not reversible continuity. Different move would need a form that is not a block/band with a jog; this direction has now failed twice, drop it.
